question: Why is our auto business shrinking this year?

grade.reason: Nothing to find: needs the LLM grader (Phase 3).

report.interpretation: I read 'shrinking' as a fall in the size of the auto book, meaning policies in force and earned premium (exposure_monthly, product = auto). I compared Jan–Sep 2026 with Jan–Sep 2025 and looked at the month-by-month trend. I also checked auto claim counts, in case 'shrinking' meant claim volume.
report.answer: The data doesn't show the auto business shrinking. Average auto policies in force rose from about 29,846 (Jan–Sep 2025) to about 30,172 (Jan–Sep 2026), up about 1.1%. Earned premium rose from $22.30M to $22.54M, up about 1.1%. Policies in force grew in almost every month, from 30,075 in Jan 2026 to 30,269 in Sep 2026. Growth is small and steady, and every region is flat to slightly up. Auto claim counts aren't falling either. They run roughly 190–245 a month, with a July 2026 spike to 344. September 2026 shows only 173 claims, but that month is incomplete: about 79% of its claims have probably been reported so far. If you saw a drop somewhere, it was probably that incomplete latest month, or a different measure. Tell me which report or metric you saw and I'll look at it.
report.answer_sql: SELECT year(month) AS yr, round(sum(policies_in_force)/count(DISTINCT month)) AS avg_policies_in_force, round(sum(earned_premium)) AS earned_premium FROM exposure_monthly WHERE product='auto' AND (month BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-09-30' OR month BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-09-30') GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

hypotheses.hypothesis: Auto exposure (policies in force) is declining
hypotheses.evidence: Policies in force rose in nearly every month, from 30,075 in Jan 2026 to 30,269 in Sep 2026.
Monthly auto earned premium rose from $2.496M in Jan 2026 to $2.512M in Sep 2026.
Counts are flat to noisy and Sep 2026 is incomplete. Frequency is therefore not clearly changing, and it isn't a measure of business size anyway.

data_quality_issues.issue: The latest loss month (Sep 2026) is incomplete because claims are reported late (about 79% reported).
data_quality_issues.impact: Claim counts for Sep 2026 look artificially low and could be misread as shrinkage.

SELECT CAST(date_trunc('month', month) AS DATE) AS period, sum(policies_in_force) / count(DISTINCT month) AS value
FROM source
WHERE month >= DATE '2025-01-01'

  AND product IN ('auto')
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY ALL
